findings.title: Accessibility Service Combined with System Overlay
findings.description: The application declares both an AccessibilityService and the SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission.
findings.assessment: The combination of AccessibilityService and System Overlay provides the technical capability for UI redressing, credential harvesting, and tapjacking.
limitations: Assistive technology and automation utilities may legitimately combine overlays and accessibility services.
references: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

findings.title: OS Command Execution Capability Detected
findings.description: Application references process execution APIs (Runtime.exec orProcessBuilder)or shell invocation binary strings.
findings.assessment: The application contains code paths capable of executing operatingsystem commandsor spawning shell processes.
limitations: Terminal emulators, system utilities, and hardware diagnostic librarieslegitimately execute shell commands.
references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

findings.title: Dynamic Class Loading Capability Detected
findings.description: Application references DexClassLoader, PathClassLoader, orInMemoryDexClassLoaderto load bytecode dynamically.
findings.assessment: The application possesses the capability to load and execute DEXbytecode from externalfiles or memory buffers at runtime.
limitations: Dynamic class loading is used legitimately by plugin frameworks,hotpatch systems, and game engines.
references: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

findings.title: Dynamic Bytecode Loading Capability
findings.description: The application references Android dynamic class loading mechanisms (DexClassLoader or PathClassLoader).
findings.assessment: The APK references APIs capable of loading executable DEX code dynamically from files or memory at runtime.
limitations: Dynamic loading is used by plugin architectures, hotpatch frameworks, and some game engines.
references: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

findings.title: Local Command Execution Capability
findings.description: The application references command execution APIs such as Runtime.getRuntime().exec() or ProcessBuilder.
findings.assessment: The APK contains static references allowing execution of shell commands or native child processes.
limitations: Static command execution references may exist in legitimate developer tools or diagnostic libraries.
references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

findings.assessment: High entropy indicates non-plaintext data. Combined with dynamicloading or reflection,this pattern is often associated with encrypted secondary payloads.
limitations: Legitimate applications encrypt proprietary game assets, databases,and configuration files.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Capabilities Co-Occur with External NetworkCommunication
findings.description: The APK combines sensitive data access capabilities (e.g. location,contacts, device IDs)with HTTP networking clients and external domains.
findings.assessment: The technical capability exists to transmit accessed sensitivedevice informationto external servers.
limitations: Static analysis cannot prove that data retrieved by sensitive APIsis actuallyserialized and sent in the network payload.
references: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information

findings.title: Accessibility Service Implementation
findings.description: The application declares an AccessibilityService component.
findings.assessment: The APK declares an AccessibilityService capable of inspecting UI windows and user actions.
limitations: Accessibility services require explicit user approval in system settings before running.

findings.title: Android Accessibility Service Implementation
findings.description: Application implements an AccessibilityService component.
findings.assessment: Accessibility Services possess broad permissions to inspect screencontent, inject gestures,and read text across all applications on the device.
limitations: Accessibility services are an essential Android feature for assistivetechnologies, screen readers, and automation.

findings.title: Phone Call State & Log Monitoring Capability
findings.description: The application requests phone state permissions and references telephony manager APIs.
findings.assessment: The APK contains capabilities to monitor telephony state and phone call activity.
limitations: Static presence of TelephonyManager does not prove call eavesdropping or logging.
references: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information

findings.title: Hardware & Persistent Device Identifier Collection Capability
findings.description: Application references persistent hardware identifiers (IMEI, IMSI,Serial Number, or Android ID).

evidence.description: Telephony hardware identifier method reference: getImei
Telephony hardware identifier method reference: getSubscriberIdForSubscriber
Telephony hardware identifier method reference: getSubscriberIds
Telephony hardware identifier method reference: getDeviceIdleController
Telephony hardware identifier method reference: getDeviceId

findings.assessment: The APK queries non-resettable hardware identifiers, which allowpersistent cross-installand cross-application device tracking that bypasses user privacy controls.
limitations: Legacy SDKs and device management tools frequently query hardwareidentifiers for licensing.
references: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information

findings.title: System Alert Window (Overlay) Capability
findings.description: The application requests the SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW permission allowing display over other applications.
findings.assessment: The APK requests permissions to display windows on top of all other applications (tapjacking / overlay risk).
limitations: Overlay capability is legitimate for utilities, floating chats, and screen tools.
references: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

findings.title: Device Boot Persistence Mechanism Detected
findings.description: Application requests RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED permission and/or declares broadcast receivers listening for device boot completion.
findings.assessment: The application contains components configured to automatically startor resume executionwhen the device is powered on or rebooted.
limitations: Boot startup is standard for communication apps, alarm managers, andscheduled synchronization services.

findings.title: Root Environment Query / Su Reference Detected
findings.description: Application references root environment paths or management binaries(e.g. su, Superuser, Magisk).
findings.assessment: The application checks for device rooting or references root utilitybinaries.This may indicate either anti-root self-defense checks or root-privilege escalation attempts.
limitations: Banking and security applications frequently contain root-checking codefor environmental integrity verification.

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP URL References Detected
findings.description: Discovered 20 unencrypted HTTP URLs in theapplication.
findings.assessment: Using plain HTTP allows network adversaries on the same path (e.g.public Wi-Fi)to monitor or modify transmitted data.
limitations: Static URL strings may be fallback endpoints or legacy protocoldocumentation references.
references: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

findings.title: Background Clipboard Access Capability
findings.description: The application references ClipboardManager within background execution components.
findings.assessment: The APK contains static references to clipboard access in a background service context.
limitations: Static reference does not prove unprompted clipboard reading during runtime.

findings.title: Application Backup Enabled Without Restriction
findings.description: The AndroidManifest.xml has android:allowBackup="true" without restrictive backup rules, allowing adb backup.
findings.assessment: Application private data can be extracted using ADB backup if physical or debugging access is gained.
limitations: System backup is standard for user data migration; risk depends on sensitivity of stored credentials.

findings.title: Legacy Cryptographic Hash Algorithm Referenced (MD5/SHA-1)
findings.description: Application references deprecated hash algorithms: SHA-1.

evidence.description: Weak hash algorithm referenced in io.github.muntashirakon.AppManager.apk.signing.Signer: SHA-1

findings.assessment: MD5 and SHA-1 have proven collision attacks. If used for digital signatures or password verification, they can be bypassed by practical collision generation.
limitations: MD5 and SHA-1 are frequently used for non-cryptographic cache keys or file integrity checksums.

findings.title: Exported Broadcast Receiver Lacks Permission Protection
findings.description: Found 4 Broadcast Receiver(s) declared with android:exported='true' without permission constraints.
findings.assessment: Any application on the device can send broadcast intents to thisreceiver,potentially triggering internal workflows with forged parameters.
limitations: Receivers listening to system broadcasts (e.g. connectivity changes)must be exported.
references: CWE-926: Improper Export of Android Application Components

findings.title: Application Data Backup Enabled (allowBackup=true)
findings.description: The application manifest sets android:allowBackup='true'. Application private databases and shared preferences can be backed upvia ADB.
findings.assessment: Anyone with physical access to an unlocked device or ADB authorizationcan run 'adb backup'to extract the application's internal files and local credentials.
limitations: Google Drive auto-backup relies on allowBackup; applications may useandroid:fullBackupContent rules.

findings.title: Weak Cryptographic Hash Algorithm Referenced
findings.description: The application references legacy hash functions (MD5 or SHA-1).
findings.assessment: MD5 and SHA-1 have known collision vulnerabilities. If used for cryptographic signatures or password hashing, they represent a weakness.
limitations: MD5 and SHA-1 are frequently used for non-cryptographic checksums or cache keys, which does not constitute a vulnerability.

findings.title: Foreground Service Declaration
findings.description: Application declares Android Foreground Service components withexplicit types.
findings.assessment: Foreground services run with elevated priority and are less likely tobe terminatedby the Android system during low-memory conditions.
limitations: Foreground services require persistent user notifications and arestandard for media players and GPS navigation.
